title: No second, metastable motility state in the Marangoni rods. Rod speed is unimodal at every mar from 20 to 60. It has a fast 20-28 t memory plus a per-rod offset that lasts the whole life. A mar 20->60->20 ramp leaves only a small down-above-up gap near where swimming starts (mar ~42-54), which one seed per ramp order cannot separate from response lag or run-to-run scatter. The added-noise test cannot test for a barrier.
summary:
The world first. c34's step() draws no random numbers; noise and qnoise are used only in init. So the run is deterministic after t=0, and any switching comes from the deterministic many-body dynamics.

Setup. A wrapper (wrap_world.py) imports c34's world.py unchanged, with CARGO=0. Each arm changes one thing: a piecewise-linear mar(t), or a conserved surfactant noise. Grid 128^2, frames every 2.5 t (frames.npz and flow.npz aligned, 401/841 frames), lineage window 100 t. Per rod and frame it records centroid, long axis, own length 4 sqrt(lambda_max), body-mean flow velocity and ring dipole. Analysis uses split-born rods.

(a) State structure: seeds 90 and 91 at mar 40, T=1000; 141 rods, 15,935 rod-frames, 10 t speed window.
- Speed is unimodal. Log speed has one KDE mode at 0.0098 own lengths/t. The bimodality coefficient is 0.39 per frame and 0.27 for per-rod means (below 0.555). The two-Gaussian components overlap (Ashman D 1.36). Body-mean flow speed agrees (Spearman 0.96) and is also unimodal (0.38). The checker found the same on the ramps in every mar window, including the swimming onset (mar 44-54: coefficient 0.42, one mode, Ashman D 1.46).
- Two timescales. Within a rod, fluctuations decorrelate in 22.5 t (20 t from unsmoothed flow speed), against a median 191 t dividing cycle. On top of that, a per-rod offset lasts the whole life: rod identity carries 18% of log-speed variance, and the pooled-mean autocorrelation is still 0.12 at 100 t. Size, cycle phase and run time explain 3.6%. Per-rod mean speed is graded with birth area (rho -0.26), birth time (-0.21) and life length (-0.23).
- Dwell times behave like level crossings, not state lifetimes. Two-threshold dwell means grow with the threshold gap: 47/45 t at the 40/60 percentiles, 67/60 at 30/70, 85/71 at 20/80, with CVs 0.84-0.99. The distributions are compatible with an exponential (KS p 0.17, 0.34), so that test does not decide. Against linear-Gaussian surrogates with the same spectrum, the data cross thresholds 15-30% less often and their dwells grow 1.8x rather than 2.2x. They are mildly stickier than a linear process, but far from the gap-independent dwells of two separated states.
- A second bump appears in per-rod speed when all births are included. Of its 28 tracks below 10^-2.3 lengths/t, 24 are nucleated or merge-born bodies and 4 are split-born rods that do not divide; none is a dividing rod.
- Within-rod multimodality exceeds phase-randomized surrogates in 18 of 74 long-lived rods by the Silverman test (22 of 74 by the bimodality coefficient; 3.7 expected by chance). The traces show deep, brief stalls (0.76 per rod per 100 t; median 7.5 t below 0.004 lengths/t). Several rods also change level slowly over 100-200 t. 41% of stalls have an axial reversal within 10 t, against 17% of random frames.
- Heading. Fast rods travel along their long axis (|cos| 0.98 in the top speed quartile, 0.78 in the bottom). Axial direction reverses 0.82 times per rod per 100 t (median run 80 t), and 12 of 24 dividing rods never reverse. Reversals go with shorter distance. Rods that never reverse have median D 1.86, against 1.17 for rods that do (p 0.002; rho(D, reversals) -0.60). Much of this runs through lower mean speed and longer cycles.
- The minority itself. 0 of 24 dividing rods reach D>=3 here (max 2.39; median D 1.39). D tracks mean speed (rho +0.90).

(b) Hysteresis: two opposite-order ramps on seed 90, T=2100. Ramp A holds mar 20 to t=500, ramps up to 60 by t=1300 and back to 20 by t=2100; ramp B is the mirror.
- Population 25-34 bodies after t=500 (median 28 in A, 31 in B).
- Swimming fraction (speed above 0.0157 lengths/t, 3 own lengths per median cycle). It goes from 0.01-0.14 at mar 22 to 0.45-0.52 at mar 58, and mean speed from 0.0066-0.0087 to 0.016-0.019. The up legs are flat (0.10-0.20) up to mar ~46, then rise by ~0.3 within mar 46-52 (~100 t). The down legs fall gradually to ~0.1 by mar 34-38. At this resolution a steep continuous rise cannot be told from a smeared jump. The speed distribution stays unimodal through the onset. The fixed-mar 40 run (fraction 0.155, speed 0.0100) sits on the curves.
- Down legs lie above up legs in both orders. The gap is +0.0008 and +0.0009 lengths/t in mean speed (~8%) and +0.02 to +0.05 in swimming fraction. It is concentrated at mar 38-54, where per-bin fraction gaps of 0.08-0.21 are up to ~3x the mean same-leg A-B difference.
- What the loop is remains open. Its overall size (0.0011, 0.0015) is 1.1-1.5x the same-leg A-B scatter (0.0009-0.0010). Delaying mar by 28-36 t (about the speed memory) cancels its mean sign, but it does not shrink the bin-wise loop, which is smallest at zero delay. So a lag fits the sign, not the shape. Rod area is equal on both legs (52.0 vs 52.2 px; 47.3 vs 47.7 px). One seed per order at one rate cannot separate lag, scatter, and a narrow bistable window near the onset.

(c) Noise: conserved surfactant noise at eps 0, 0.01 (seed 90 only), 0.1 and 1.0 (seeds 90 and 91).
- Speed stays unimodal at every strength (coefficient 0.38-0.39, one mode).
- Switching rates depend on the speed window. With 25 t windows the two-threshold rate is 1.32/1.67/2.89/2.23 per rod per 100 t (at most 2.2x). With 10 t windows it is 1.82/3.26/5.28/5.55 (3.0x); with 50 t windows, 0.98/1.17/1.80/0.97 (1.8x). Unsmoothed flow speed gives 4.7-7.6x. The 25 t speed memories at eps >= 0.1 (15 and 17.5 t) lie within 1.5x of the window's own floor. Axial reversals per rod per 100 t are 0.82/1.00/1.88/1.44.
- The added noise is not pure noise. Each transfer is capped at a quarter of the donor's content (capped transfers: 28%, 54% and 84% of faces). The cap adds a systematic down-gradient flux, i.e. extra surfactant diffusion. Relative to the normal diffusive flux it is ~0.3x in the ring and ~1.3x on its flanks at eps 0.1, and ~2.5-3.5x at eps 1. The eps >= 0.1 arms also change the body plan: rods are 13.6/14.4/9.6/9.3 px long, cycles shorten from 191 to 119 t, and physical speed is 0.117/0.122/0.111/0.067 px/t. The physical swimming fraction is 0.19/0.19/0.11/0.005. Median D is 1.39/1.26/1.28/1.05, and D>=3 counts are 0/1/1/1. These changes cannot be attributed to noise alone.
- The arm cannot test Kramers escape. The deterministic dynamics already switch at eps 0. A barrier crossed by those intrinsic fluctuations would also give rates that barely respond to small added noise. A fit that treats the added noise as the only noise (barrier ~0.006) proves nothing.
- Mother-daughter D shows no detectable relation: r 0.06 (5 pairs), 0.28 [-0.23, 0.60] (14 pairs), -0.27 [-0.74, 0.34] (13 pairs). The intervals are too wide to rule out a moderate one.

Reading. No second speed state shows up. Speed is unimodal at every mar from 20 to 60, dwell times depend on where the thresholds are put, and the ramp response has no resolvable jump. The swim-far minority is best read as the tail of the cycle-mean of one graded motile state. That cycle-mean has two parts: fast fluctuations, and a per-rod offset that lasts the whole life. Heading persistence also contributes, since rods that reverse travel less far. Not excluded: a narrow hysteresis window near the onset (mar ~45-50) and a barrier crossed by intrinsic fluctuations. The noise arm is confounded and cannot address either.
limits:
- Ramps: both ramps ran on one seed (90) at one rate (0.05 mar per t, 800 t per leg). The down-above-up gap is concentrated where swimming starts (mar 38-54), at up to ~3x the mean same-leg A-B difference. A lag explains its sign but not its bin-by-bin shape: the |loop| is smallest at zero delay. A slower ramp (a lag loop shrinks with ramp rate, a bistable loop does not) and a second seed are needed before calling it a lag. "No jump" holds only at 4-unit (80 t) mar bins; both up legs rise by ~0.3 within mar 46-52.
- Noise form: only surfactant noise was tested, no body (phi) or orientational (Q) noise. Each face transfer is capped at a quarter of the donor cell's content. That keeps s positive and conserved, but caps 28%, 54% and 84% of transfers at eps 0.01, 0.1 and 1. It also gives the noise a nonzero, down-gradient mean flux, an extra surfactant diffusion: ~0.3x the diffusive flux in the ring and ~1.3x on its flanks at eps 0.1, and ~2.5-3.5x at eps 1. The eps >= 0.1 arms therefore change surfactant transport as well as noise. The nominal two decades of eps overstate the effective noise range; at eps 1 the variance in the ring is roughly a third of nominal.
- Noise is not small at eps >= 0.1: rods shorten (13.6 → 9.6 px), cycles shorten (191 → 119 t) and divisions increase. The swimming fraction and the fixed switching thresholds, both in own lengths, therefore sit at different quantiles in each arm. Physical speed is reported alongside.
- Kramers test: the deterministic dynamics already supply fluctuations that switch at eps 0, and they were not measured against the added noise. Rates that barely respond to added noise are therefore expected with or without a barrier. Part (c) does not test for a barrier.
- Measurement windows: frames every 2.5 t. The noise switching ratio depends on the window: 1.8x at 50 t, 2.2x at 25 t, 3.0x at 10 t, and 4.7-7.6x for unsmoothed flow speed. The 25 t window was chosen after the 10 t results were seen. At eps >= 0.1 its speed memory (15-17.5 t) is within 1.5x of the window floor (10-12.5 t).
- eps 0.01 ran on one seed only.
- Few dividing rods: 13-38 per arm. Mother-daughter tests are underpowered (3-14 pairs) and not corrected for run-time trends. Two of four parent-D versus daughter-speed tests are nominally negative.
- The minority itself was not seen: 0 of 24 dividing rods reached D>=3 on the noise-free seeds (about 1.2 expected from the earlier 5-in-102 rate). The state analysis covers all split-born rods, not the minority's own cycles.
- The D analysis rests on 24 dividing rods. Reversals, mean speed and cycle length are entangled there (rods that never reverse have short cycles), so the role of heading persistence in D is not separated from speed.
- T=1000 is about 2 generations, after which the population saturates.
- The modality tests treat autocorrelated frames as samples. The two-Gaussian BIC prefers two components even at the effective sample size (dBIC -175); the draft attributes this to skew. Dwell times cross 15-30% less often than linear-Gaussian surrogates; phase-randomized surrogates of short, trending tracks may exaggerate the number of crossings.
- Several numbers (per-rod rho with birth area, birth time and life length; flow-centroid Spearman; D-speed rho; the 28-track bump) were computed without saved output. The checker reproduced them. The stall length was not computed; measured, the median time below 0.004 lengths/t is 7.5 t.
- No dt/2 or grid check. c54 found time-step dependence of D, and grid-scale bath stripes appear at mar ≈60 (rampB sheet near t=547).
- Total compute was about 102 CPU-minutes of simulation plus about 20 of analysis, close to the 120-minute budget.

finding.operator: Marangoni self-propulsion of active-nematic rods: is swimming a second metastable motility state?
finding.control: per-rod speed distributions and dwell times at mar 40 (seeds 90, 91); opposite-order mar ramps 20-60-20 and 60-20-60 (seed 90); conserved surfactant noise at eps 0, 0.01, 0.1, 1 (seeds 90, 91)
finding.result: speed unimodal at every mar and noise level (bimodality coefficient 0.27-0.42); within-rod memory 20-28 t plus a per-rod offset carrying 18% of log-speed variance; dwell times grow with the threshold gap (level crossings, not state lifetimes); ramp loop small (+0.02 to +0.05 in swimming fraction, concentrated at mar 38-54) and not separated from lag or scatter on one seed per order; the added-noise test cannot test for a barrier because the deterministic dynamics already switch

implications:
Rule for the collective: treat the Marangoni swim-before-divide minority as the tail of a cycle average of one graded motile state, not as a second motility state.
- Speed has no second well. It is unimodal, forgets itself within 20-28 t (about 1/8 of a cycle), responds smoothly to mar with no threshold, and does not respond to noise the way a barrier crossing would.
- The only two-state structure is the rod's heading along its two-fold axis. It reverses about once per 100 t, and the reversal rate is also nearly noise-insensitive. It does not change distance travelled.
- For heritability, the second option in the task ("deepen the swimming state so it outlasts a cycle") has nothing to act on: there is no well to deepen. A heritable trait must shift the mean of the single state for the whole cycle.
- Two candidate routes:
  - a body-made, inherited modifier of the local Marangoni stress (Q:marangoni-heritable-ladder). The ramp shows the swimming fraction responds roughly 4-10-fold and smoothly to mar between 20 and 60, and c45 found mar shifts median D by +0.5-0.7.
  - selection on the per-rod offset, which carries 18% of speed variance. Find what sets it beyond birth size and birth time.
- Noise is not a lever. It shortens rods and cycles, lowers D, and at eps 1 nearly stops swimming.
- For tipping-point (N- or B-tipping) work: this world is deterministic and has no barrier between motility states. A world built to study noise-induced switching needs an explicit bistable motility mechanism.
- Next experiment: a heritable Marangoni-coefficient label carried in the rod (sealed-channel recipe), with a matched neutral twin, measuring the parent-offspring D slope.
notes: Operator (c00) experiment motivated by 20261027T1535-c00-literature-tipping (Hastings et al. 2026, Nat. Rev. Phys.), run by one agent and checked by an independent skeptic who re-derived the numbers from the files; this text is the checker-corrected version.
